title: U.S. House · Illinois's 8th District
area: Northwest Chicago suburbs in Cook County, including Schaumburg, Hoffman Estates, Elk Grove Village and Palatine.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Raja Krishnamoorthi is running for U.S. Senate rather than seeking re-election here. Melissa Bean, who represented this district in Congress from 2005 to 2011, won an eight-way March 17, 2026 Democratic primary. Jennifer Davis won the Republican primary. Ballotpedia calculated the district's Cook Partisan Voter Index as D+5, based on the 2020 and 2024 presidential elections.

summary.text: Melissa Bean is the Democratic nominee for the open Illinois 8th District seat, which she represented in Congress from 2005 to 2011. A former home-based business owner who served as a member of the Blue Dog and New Democrat coalitions, she lost the seat in 2010, later worked in finance and business leadership (JPMorgan Chase, Mesirow Financial), and won the March 2026 Democratic primary. According to her campaign website, she is running on housing, healthcare, energy and education costs, workforce training, and support for workers and small business owners.

background.text: Born Melissa Luburich on January 22, 1962, in Chicago, she grew up in a Serbian-American family in the Chicago suburbs.
Attended Maine East High School, earned an associate degree from Oakton Community College in 1982, and earned a bachelor's degree from Roosevelt University in 2000.
Before elected office, was president of a home-based business, Sales Resources Inc.

Ran for the 8th District seat in 2002, losing to Republican incumbent Phil Crane with 43 percent of the vote, and defeated Crane in a 2004 rematch with 52 percent. When she took office on January 3, 2005, she became the first Democrat to represent the district since it was formed in 1935.

Served in the U.S. House from 2005 to 2011 as a member of the Blue Dog Coalition and the New Democrat Coalition, with seats on the Financial Services and Small Business committees. She lost her 2010 re-election bid to Republican Joe Walsh by 291 votes.
As a member of Congress, voted for the Affordable Care Act, TARP, the 2009 stimulus bill, the auto industry bailout, the 'Cash for Clunkers' program, and cap-and-trade climate legislation.

In 2011 became president and CEO of the Executives Club of Chicago, later served as chair of Midwest operations for JPMorgan Chase, and became CEO of Mesirow Wealth Advisors, part of Mesirow Financial, in 2019. Ballotpedia also lists affiliations with One Million Degrees, Junior Achievement and World Business Chicago.

Announced in September 2025 that she would seek her former seat after Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi entered the U.S. Senate race, and won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary with 31.6% of the vote in a field of eight.
Wikipedia reports she lives in unincorporated Palatine Township with her husband, Alan Bean; the page notes the residence detail needs updating.

priorities.text: Says she would protect and strengthen the Affordable Care Act, including protections for pre-existing conditions, and allow Medicare to negotiate prescription drug prices directly.

Says masked ICE agents have been deployed unnecessarily into communities and calls for DHS Secretary Kristi Noem's firing or removal, greater ICE oversight including body cameras, and accountability for agents who exceed their authority.
Says she would codify Roe v. Wade protections, expand healthcare privacy protections, and oppose any federal abortion ban.

positions.summary: Voted for the Affordable Care Act while in Congress and says she would protect and strengthen it, including allowing Medicare to negotiate drug prices.
Says she would work to codify Roe v. Wade protections and oppose any federal abortion ban.
Calls for greater ICE oversight and accountability, and opposes what she describes as unnecessary deployment of masked ICE agents into communities.
Says she has a record of supporting science-based climate policy and will work to cut emissions and scale clean energy.
Campaign platform emphasizes closing wealth gaps through worker profit-sharing and pension incentives, without a direct statement on raising taxes on high earners or corporations.

record.text: As a member of Congress in 2009-2010, voted with the House Democratic leadership 90.8% of the time according to a July 2010 analysis, and voted for TARP, the 2009 stimulus bill, the auto bailout, 'Cash for Clunkers,' cap-and-trade, and the Affordable Care Act.

summary.text: Jennifer Davis is the Republican nominee for Illinois's 8th District and a first-time candidate for federal office. She co-founded the software company Davisware and later launched BExponential, and describes herself as a political outsider. She won the March 2026 Republican primary and, in her Ballotpedia survey, names affordability, small-business support and cybersecurity as her main messages.

background.text: Describes herself as having co-founded the service-technology software company Davisware with her husband, Dan, at age 17, and growing it into a global company.

According to her Ballotpedia survey, she guided Davisware through the pandemic and a partnership with Serent Capital, then launched BExponential, a business to help women thrive personally and professionally.
Wrote a book, "Living Exponentially in Life and Business."
Describes herself as a mother of ten, a coach of dozens of youth teams, and a community servant with rural values of hard work, faith and family.
Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 51.4% of the vote, ahead of Mark Rice (40.2%), Kevin Ake and Herbert Hebein.
Her Ballotpedia survey lists affordability, support for small businesses and entrepreneurs, and a proposed "Digital Dome" cyber defense program among her key messages.

priorities.text: Says affordability is the top issue in the district and pledges to cut federal taxes on working families and ease regulations on small businesses.
Says she would champion policies to help small businesses, which she says employ 44% of Illinois's workforce, by cutting taxes and streamlining regulations.

Proposes a "Digital Dome" national cybersecurity shield to protect families and the military from cyberattacks and online predators, and supports expanding U.S. oil, gas and renewable energy production.

positions.summary: Pledges to cut federal taxes on working families and ease regulations on small businesses and entrepreneurs.
Says she would drive energy independence by expanding U.S. oil, gas and renewable production to cut reliance on other countries.
